images.title: Copies that fill the chikki
images.purpose: Show that a piece is named by how many equal copies of it fill the whole: 8 copies of a 3 square piece fill the chikki, so it is 1/8.
images.composition: One piece standing on the left, and the chikki filled with its numbered copies on the right, with wide space between.
images.exact_structure: Left: one piece, a row of 3 small squares across and 1 down, filled teal #0072B2. Right: one chikki drawn as a grid of 24 equal small squares, 6 across and 4 down, with a dashed grey #6B7280 outline of the whole. It is filled by 8 copies of the piece, 2 copies in each of the 4 rows, each copy outlined amber #E69F00 and numbered 1 to 8. Exactly 1 piece, 1 grid, 8 copies.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any on-screen control, panel or app interface drawn in the frame
images.takeaway: The number of equal copies that fill the whole names the piece.
images.description: A piece of 3 small squares beside a 6 by 4 chikki grid filled by 8 numbered copies of it, so the piece is 1/8 of the chikki.
images.context: Shown with the doer concept before the student practises. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the numbered copies and say the name of the piece, 1 over that count.

image_decisions.why: Numbered copies of one piece filling the chikki show the one idea the practice uses: count copies to name the piece.
